sections.html:
Fairfield sits on the Sound west of Bridgeport, with Trumbull, Easton, Weston and Westport as its other neighbors. The 2020 count was 61,512 people, and the 2024 estimate is 65,300. The town covers 31.38 square miles and uses ZIP codes 06824, 06825 and 06828.

Buyers here shop by section rather than by town: Southport, Greenfield Hill, Stratfield, Tunxis Hill, Grasmere, Mill Plain, Holland Hill and the Fairfield Beach area all price differently. With three Metro-North stops (Fairfield-Black Rock, Fairfield and Southport) plus U.S. 1, I-95 and the Merritt, commuter buyers measure the walk to a platform or the drive to an on-ramp.

Fairfield has about 5 miles of Long Island Sound coastline, five lifeguarded town beaches and a good number of tidal creeks, so plenty of houses sit near water. Rivers and brooks cross town too, among them the Mill, the Rooster, Ash Creek and Sasco Brook, and newer homes keep going up in the Fairfield Beach area close to the sand.

Houses by the water draw questions an inland house never gets. Settle these before you pick a listing date.

  • Ask your lender or insurer whether the lot is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Note how old any bulkhead, seawall or septic system is.
  • Gather elevation and insurance history, since buyers on low streets ask for both.

For a particular address, the town building office is the place to ask.

Real estate tax comes in four payments a year. A bill totaling $100 or less is collected in one piece with the first installment. The Tax Collector's warning is blunt: never set a bill aside. Interest keeps growing until it is paid or the Tax Assessor takes it off, and a bill lost in the mail does not excuse a late payment.

Bill typeDue dates
Real estateJuly 1, October 1, January 1, April 1
Motor vehicleJuly 1 each year
Supplemental motor vehicleJanuary 1
Business personal propertyJuly 1 and January 1
Sewer use, bills over $300October 1 and April 1

The full calendar is on the town's tax due dates page.

Disputes over value go to the Board of Assessment Appeals. On the 2026 Grand List the petition must be received at the Assessor's Office by 4:30 pm on Friday, February 19, 2027. A postmark earns you nothing. The town's appeals page has the form.

Email to assessor@fairfieldct.org is accepted. Each property needs its own petition, real estate filings should include the property card, and anyone speaking for you needs a notarized affidavit.

  • Hearing notices go out by mail on or before March 1, and hearings are held through the month.
  • You get 15 minutes, and testimony is sworn and recorded.
  • The Board votes later at a separate meeting.
  • The Board may raise a value as well as cut it, so file only if your evidence is strong.
  • Still unhappy? Superior Court is the next step, with 60 days from the mailed notice to apply.

The Board has used state law to skip hearings on commercial properties assessed over $1,000,000. Owners of those go straight to court.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax at the closing table
sections.html:
Selling a Fairfield house adds a state filing to the local tax bill. The conveyance tax return, Form OP-236, goes in with the recorded deed, and the seller, the seller's lawyer or an agent can file it. Consideration of $2,000 or more is taxable unless an exemption applies. Fairfield's code on the form is 051.

Two exemptions matter most to owners under pressure. One is a deed given in lieu of foreclosure on your own residence. The other is a sale of that residence for less than the mortgages plus the tax liens that outrank them. The state's conveyance tax page carries the complete list. The actual Fairfield figure comes from your closing agent.

An open balance does not stop a sale. Proceeds cover what is still due, so you can list the house or hand it over as-is without writing a check first. Work through these steps in order.

  1. Call the Tax Collector and ask which quarterly installments are paid and which are open.
  2. Ask whether sewer use is billed on the property. That bill runs on its own October and April calendar.
  3. Give the numbers to your closing attorney or title company so the payoff lands on the settlement statement.
  4. Choose a closing date with the quarterly calendar in view, because one installment is often part open at transfer.
  5. Bring photo ID and any estate papers to the closing if the house was inherited.

If a bill never reached you, still call. The tax and its interest stand even when the mail failed, and the office can read you the balance.

sections.h2: Waiting on probate or a tenant lease
sections.html: Two situations stretch a Fairfield timeline more than any repair. An estate has to name someone with authority to sign the deed, and the quarterly bills keep coming in the meantime. Ask the Tax Collector to mail copies to the executor so nothing slips by unnoticed while the estate is open. A rented house works differently: the tenant's lease usually runs past your preferred closing, so find out early whether the tenant plans to stay or leave, and put the answer in writing before you accept an offer.

Aging houses on small lots, shoreline worries and a four-part tax calendar are the usual story. A house near the beach can carry deferred maintenance, so many owners order an inspection before they list. An inherited house may sit through several due dates while the estate settles who owns it. If tenants live there, the lease has to be dealt with before closing.

A cash sale skips most of that. The buyer takes the house as it stands, you do not schedule showings or fund repairs, and the title company settles any open tax from the proceeds. Weigh that against what repairs, showings and one more installment would cost you.

sections.h2: Getting ready for the Assessor's Office
sections.html:
If you plan to appeal before selling, a lower assessment can help the next owner and your own final bills. Pull your property card first and read it line by line. Wrong square footage, an extra bathroom or a finished basement that was never finished are the common errors. Bring photos and any recent sale prices for similar houses on your street.

Keep one folder for the petition, the card, your evidence and the date you filed. If you are not the owner of record, for example an executor, gather the authority papers before the hearing so the 15 minutes goes to the case rather than to paperwork.

faqs.q: When are Fairfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due quarterly on July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1. A bill of $100 or less is due in full with the first installment.

faqs.q: What is the Fairfield appeal deadline?
faqs.a: For the 2026 Grand List, petitions must reach the Assessor's Office by 4:30 pm on Friday, February 19, 2027. Postmarks do not count, but email to assessor@fairfieldct.org is allowed.

faqs.q: How long is a Fairfield assessment hearing?
faqs.a: Each hearing is 15 minutes, with sworn and recorded testimony. The Board decides later at a separate meeting and can raise or lower the assessment.

faqs.q: What is Fairfield's town code on the conveyance form?
faqs.a: The code is 051 on Form OP-236, the state conveyance tax return filed when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fairfield house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Your proceeds cover the open balance at closing, so an as-is sale works even when installments are still due.
